question: A 40-year-old patient is referred at 16 weeks with persistent pain and an ununited clavicle fracture. Which fracture site carries the highest inherent non-union risk and therefore most commonly requires operative intervention?

answers.text: Middle third (Allman Group I) with minimal displacement

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Undisplaced or minimally displaced middle-third fractures have a very low non-union rate (<1%).

answers.text: Lateral third (Allman Group II, Neer Type II) with disrupted coracoclavicular ligaments

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Neer Type II lateral third fractures have the highest non-union rate (~30%) because the coracoclavicular ligaments remain attached to the distal fragment, creating a deforming force and gap.
Medial third fractures are rare. Non-union at this site is uncommon; the main concern is proximity to mediastinal structures.

answers.text: Middle third (Allman Group I) with >20 mm shortening

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Significant shortening does increase non-union risk, but Neer Type II lateral third fractures still carry the highest absolute non-union rate (~30%).

overallFeedback.feedback: Neer Type II (lateral third, coracoclavicular ligament disrupted) fractures have the highest non-union rate (~30%) — not middle-third fractures, even displaced ones.
Exactly right. Neer Type II fractures of the lateral third have the highest non-union rate due to persistent distraction from deforming ligamentous forces.
